claims.text: The coupled wear-corrosion response of high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a nanostructured oxide layer.
The nanostructured oxide layer is dynamically replenished during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The nanostructured oxide layer enhances mechanical strength.
Dynamic oxide-layer replenishment mitigates degradation under tribo-corrosion.
The proposed mechanism produces lower total degradation than an untreated high-entropy-alloy surface.
The proposed mechanism provides balanced wear resistance and corrosion resistance.
The prediction applies under combined high temperature, humidity, and mechanical stress.
The proposed behavior is limited to high-entropy alloys within particular compositional ranges.
Failure to observe either oxide-layer replenishment or nanostructure would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as polished, whereas the baseline is described as untreated. Polishing is itself a surface treatment, so it is unclear whether these refer to the same baseline condition.
